title: nf-boltz pipeline parameters
description: Nextflow pipeline for protein structure prediction using Boltz-1

input_output_options.title: Input/Output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data

pred_name.help_text: Only letters, numbers, underscores, and dashes allowed. Used as prefix for output files. e.g. protein_complex', 'antibody_design', 'my_prediction'

outdir.help_text: The output directory where the results will be saved. Existing results with the same prediction name will be overwritten.

input_yaml.description: Path to input YAML files or directory of YAML files. If provided, this will ignore all sequence, ligand, constraints parameters below.
input_yaml.help_text: e.g. '/path/to/input.yml'. The name of each yaml file will be used for the prediction name.

diffusion_samples.help_text: Number of independent diffusion samples to generate. More samples improve quality but increase computation time.

method.description: Method conditioning to use for prediction (default: 'x-ray crystallography').
method.help_text: Choose from: 'afdb', 'boltz-1', 'md', 'electron microscopy', 'solution-nmr', 'x-ray crystallography', or 'other'. 'Other' includes methods such as electron crystallography, epr, fiber diffraction, fluorescence transfer, infrared spectroscopy, neutron diffraction, powder diffraction, solution scattering, solid-state nmr, theoretical model, that are treated equivalently

recycling_steps.help_text: More steps generally improve accuracy but increase computation time. Default = 10, same as AlphaFold3.

sampling_steps.help_text: Number of denoising steps in the diffusion process

output_format.description: Output format for structure predictions. Default: mmcif

write_full_pae.description: Whether to save the full PAE matrix as a file

write_full_pde.description: Whether to save the full PDE matrix as a file

extra_config.help_text: Extra command-line arguments for Boltz-1 (e.g., '--msa_pairing_strategy complete --confidence_threshold 0.7')

seq1_name.help_text: Optional name used in plots. Only letters, numbers, underscores, and dashes allowed.

seq1_type.help_text: Choose the biomolecule type for sequence 1. Examples: protein, dna, rna

seq1_seq.help_text: Single-letter amino acid codes for proteins, ATCG for DNA, AUCG for RNA. Example: ADNKFNKEQQNAFYEILHLPNLTEEQRNGFIQSLKDDPSVSKEILAEAKKLNDAQAPK

seq1_chain_id.help_text: Unique single chain ID (e.g., 'A') or multiple IDs separated by commas for multiple copies (e.g., 'A,B,C'). Examples: A, B,C, H,L

seq1_mod.description: Sequence 1 modifications e.g. non-canonical amino acids

seq1_cyclic.help_text: Set to true for cyclic peptides or circular DNA/RNA

seq1_genmsa.help_text: Generate multiple sequence alignment to improve prediction accuracy

affinity_ligand_id.description: Chain ID of ligand for affinity calculations

affinity_mw_correction.description: Whether to add the Molecular Weight correction to the affinity value head.

diffusion_samples_affinity.description: The number of diffusion samples to use for affinity prediction.
diffusion_samples_affinity.help_text: More samples improve quality but increase computation time. Default: 5

sampling_steps_affinity.description: Number of sampling steps for affinity prediction

constraint_options.title: Constraint options
constraint_options.description: Define structural constraints and binding pockets

constraints_bond.help_text: Format: [chain,residue,atom][chain,residue,atom]. Separate multiple bonds with spaces. e.g. '[A,33,O][B,1,N] [H,95,SG][L,23,SG]'

constraints_pocket.description: Pocket constraints. Multiple pockets can be specified, seperated by spaces.
constraints_pocket.help_text: For each pocket, specify the ID of the binder and a list of the pocket residues/atoms. Optionally provide the max distance in Angstroms of the ligand from the pocket (default: 6), and whether to use a potential to enforce the pocket constraint (default: false). Format: '[BINDER_ID][[POCKET_CHAIN_ID,RES_IDX/ATOM_NAME],[POCKET_CHAIN_ID,RES_IDX/ATOM_NAME],...][DIST_ANGSTROM][FORCE_BOOLEAN]' e.g. '[B][[A,53],[A,57],[A,61]] [C][[A,101],[A,130]][5][true]'

contraints_contacts.description: Contact constraints provided as pairs of residues or atoms. Multiple contacts can be specified, seperated by spaces.
contraints_contacts.help_text: For each contact, provide: a pair of chain IDs and residue/atoms. Optionally provide a max distance in Angstroms (default: 6) and whether to use a potential to enforce the contact (default: false). Format: '[CHAIN_ID,RES_IDX/ATOM_NAME][CHAIN_ID,RES_IDX/ATOM_NAME][DIST_ANGSTROM][FORCE_BOOLEAN]' e.g. '[A,53][A,57] [A,101][A,130][5][true]

templates.description: Structural templates (for protein sequences only). Multiple templates can be specified, seperated by spaces.
templates.help_text: Each template block consists of a path to a CIF file, the prediction chain ID(s) to be templated, template chain ID(s), whether to use a force potential (default: false), and the distance in Angstroms that the prediction can deviate from the template (required when force=true, default='inf'). Format: '[CIF_PATH][PREDICTION_IDs][TEMPLATE_IDs][FORCE_BOOLEAN][THRESHOLD_ANGSTROM]'. If chain IDs are not provided, Boltz will automatically match prediction chains to template chains i.e. to automatically match leave one or both chain ID elements empty e.g. '['./template.cif'][][]' will match all template chains to prediction chains, '['./template.cif'][A][]' will only find templates for chain A, '['./template.cif'][][Y]' will match chain Y of template to closest prediction chain. You can explicitly map prediction chains to templates e.g. To map chain A to template chain Y, and map chain D to template chain Z '['./template.cif'][C,D][Y,Z]'. You can use the same template chain for multiple prediction chains. e.g. To map chains A and B to template chain Y, and use a potential with a threshold of 5 angstroms during prediction '['./template.cif'][A,B][Y,Y][true][5]'

gpu_model.help_text: Choose GPU model based on availability and computational requirements

n_cpus.help_text: Number of CPU cores to allocate
